questionText: Which one of the following dependencies among the register operands of different instructions can cause a data hazard in a pipelined processor?
explanation:
Step 1: Understand Data Dependencies and Hazards
Data hazards occur when an instruction depends on the result of a previous instruction that has not yet completed execution or written back its result to the register file.

Step 2: Analyze the Types of Dependencies
• Read-After-Write (RAW): A true data dependency where a subsequent instruction attempts to read a register before a prior instruction writes its updated value to it. This causes a data hazard in a standard pipelined processor.
• Read-After-Read (RAR): Both instructions read the same register, which never causes a hazard.
• Write-After-Read (WAR) & Write-After-Write (WAW): These are anti-dependencies and output dependencies (name dependencies) that can only cause hazards in out-of-order execution or superscalar architectures, not in standard in-order pipelines.

Therefore, Read-after-write can cause a data hazard (Option B).
